about: What a log line becomes on its way into a ZIP of the logs. Both redactors run every vector:
frontend/src-tauri/src/redact.rs (the Save logs ZIP, its own tests), so a rule changed in one
and not the other fails a build. The known misses are pinned too, so improving one is a
decision to change both. apiKey is the session key each vector runs with.

vectors.line: Initial sync of folder Lawyer/Divorce for j***k@seznam.cz in C:\Users\Lukas\AppData
vectors.redacted: Initial sync of folder Lawyer/Divorce for j***k@seznam.cz in C:\Users\Lukas\AppData
vectors.why: a line that keeps the rules is unchanged: an address the app masked, a folder name, a path
an address a server wrote is masked whole, its local part Unicode-aware
an apostrophe belongs to the local part
a Message-ID's '=' and '+' belong to the local part
a masked address is left: no match starts right after a '*'
no match starts right after a '*'
'/' is not in the local part, so a path in front of an address stays
followed by '-', the address falls back to the longest domain that is not: the local part is masked
followed by a digit, the same fallback
the same fallback in a Message-ID
a top-level domain running into letters and digits falls back to an earlier dot
followed by '-' with no shorter domain to fall back to, the address is left (a known miss, API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md section 5)
a combining mark after the domain is not a letter or digit, so the address is whole
a match that fails its end does not stop one starting after its '@'
no match starts right after a character an address may hold, even the end of the last match (a known miss, API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md section 5)
letters of any script, in the local part and the domain
one- and two-character local parts, masked as LogMasker masks them
an address URL-encoded as %40 is not one (a known miss, API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md section 5)
bearer credential
a no-break space is not the whitespace the bearer shape takes
Google access token
a token takes ASCII word characters only
a non-ASCII letter is not a word character, so a token right after one starts at a word boundary
Google refresh token
a refresh token right after a non-ASCII letter
no refresh token right after a '/'
no refresh token right after a word character
a refresh token refused at its start does not hide a token that starts inside it
JSON web token
Microsoft access token
XOAUTH2 initial response
OAuth parameter
OAuth parameter, quoted
an OAuth parameter value takes ASCII characters only
a non-spacing mark on a letter is part of the word for Java's \b, so no token starts after it
a non-spacing mark with no letter under it is not, so the token starts after it
the session API key
the key goes first, so what is left is no address
